dedupe_keys.name: thermos heat and cold network planning software centre for sustainable energy

description: THERMOS, the Thermal Energy Resource Modelling and Optimisation System, is web software that maps heat and cooling demand at address level and designs optimised district heating and cooling networks. The website read on 2026-09-26 says it takes building footprints and streets from OpenStreetMap or a user's GIS layers, estimates demand from building geometry, use and location, decides which buildings to connect and which streets to dig under the user's objective and constraints, models diameter-dependent pipe costs, ground heat losses and plant and storage against hourly demand, and exports GIS layers and tables. Coverage is anywhere in the world. THERMOS began as a Horizon 2020 project (grant 723636, 2016 to 2021) coordinated by the Centre for Sustainable Energy, which wrote and still maintains the software; its methods underpin the UK Government's National Zoning Model. The public tool is free after registration, the source code is published as open source for self-hosting, and users must cite the project. Caveats: demand estimates are only as good as the building data, and the licence file on GitHub could not be read because GitHub pages were blocked. Simulation uses are optimisation and capacity planning of heat networks, zoning studies and network flow and cost appraisal of expansions. Related records: platform-npro-district-energy-planning is a commercial district energy planner, and data-heat-roadmap-europe-peta4 maps heat demand in Europe.
